Title: Diagnosis of test `testLang294`
Details:

The test `testLang294` creates a `StrBuilder` instance with an initial string containing two occurrences of `"\n%BLAH%\n"` and some text lines in between. It then calls `sb.deleteAll("\n%BLAH%")`.

The `deleteAll` method is designed to remove all occurrences of the given substring (`"\n%BLAH%"`) from the `StrBuilder`. Its implementation:
- Checks the length of the substring to delete.
- Uses `indexOf(str, 0)` to find the start index of the first occurrence.
- In a loop, repeatedly calls `deleteImpl` to remove the substring found at the returned index.
- Then calls `indexOf(str, index)` again to find the next occurrence starting at the same index as the one just deleted, looping until no more occurrences (-1) are found.

The method `indexOf(String str, int startIndex)`:
- Returns the index of the first occurrence of `str` in the buffer starting at `startIndex`.
- If the substring length is 0, it returns `startIndex`.
- It uses nested loops to check characters sequentially in the buffer for a match.

The method `deleteImpl(int startIndex, int endIndex, int len)`:
- Uses `System.arraycopy` to shift characters after `endIndex` to `startIndex`.
- Decreases the `size` of the buffer by `len`.

The problem lies in the `deleteAll` method calling `indexOf(str, index)` after deleting the substring at `index`. Because the content starting at `index` has shifted left in the buffer as a result of deletion, the same position `index` is used as the start for the next search. This causes `indexOf` to skip ahead by 1 position internally (in its for-loop) and potentially miss overlapping occurrences if any.

In the test case, the substring is preceded by `\n` and contains `%BLAH%` with newlines around. Since the buffer is shifted after deletion, starting the next search at the same index results in skipping some characters that were shifted left. This could cause `deleteAll` to miss some occurrences of the substring.

Therefore, the bug is that `deleteAll` should restart searching from the same index after deletion, but the way `indexOf` is implemented, it starts just after the given start index, thus potentially missing matches after deletion due to character shifting.

Summary:
- `deleteAll` calls `indexOf(str, index)` after deletion.
- Characters shift left after deletion.
- `indexOf` loop increments index preventing checking the exact shifted position.
- Leading to missed occurrences of substring and incomplete deletion.

This causes the test `testLang294` to fail because not all occurrences of the substring `"\n%BLAH%"` are deleted as expected.

Next, I can check the exact behavior of `indexOf` method loop to confirm the skip.

org.apache.commons.lang.text.StrBuilder.indexOf(java.lang.String,int)
org.apache.commons.lang.text.StrBuilder.deleteImpl(int,int,int)
